title: terraform-gpu-nodetier-autoscaler-compat-and-upgrade-checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a single Terraform module and integration guide that supports deploying GPU node tiers inside Private (VPC) clusters and operating them with either ASG-based autoscaling or Karpenter. The module should: (1) produce launch templates/instance profiles and IAM roles for ASG flows; (2) produce Karpenter provisioner-compatible subnet/taint/tag outputs; (3) include upgrade-safe lifecycle hooks and health-check predicates for safe rolling upgrades of GPU drivers and node images; (4) expose an opt-in degraded-mode policy when GPU capacity is constrained (evict or soft-schedule noncritical jobs). This ticket is the engineering implementation + runbook + acceptance tests for production rollout in the Private environment.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes outputs: launch_template_id, autoscaler_role_arn, karpenter_provisioner_config, node_pool_tags
Module supports mixed-instance GPU pools and a constrained-fallback policy that prefers smaller GPUs when primary flavor is exhausted
Automated health checks gate node lifecycle: kubelet_ready && nvidia-smi returns devices && driver daemonset Ready
Canary rollout plan validated in staging: 3% of GPU pods routed to new node image for 24h, no SLO regressions
Upgrade runbook and automated preflight test exist and are referenced from the module README
End-to-end tests run in CI that simulate GPU driver upgrade and assert zero-data-loss and <5m pod eviction stabilization time
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — validated that Karpenter provisioner can tag nodes with 'redwood:gpu_tier' via Terraform-managed IAM role. Found edge case where Karpenter's scale-up is delayed when subnet ENI limits are reached.

2026-03-04: Decision: implement a 'capacity-fallback' config in the module that allows instances to fall back to lower-GPU-count SKUs and/or launch CPU-only pooled nodes for background workloads. This is opt-in and defaults to false for safety.

2026-03-05: Review feedback from Infra: require node-level lifecycle hook that runs a pre-drain probe to verify GPU device visibility and model server liveness before evicting pods. Also add CloudWatch/Datadog metric hooks for NodeGPUUtilization and DriverCrashLoop.

2026-03-07: Marco implemented a test fixture that deploys node image with an intentional kernel mismatch to validate driver-rollback path. Observed PodEvictionRate spike; added exponential backoff to rolling drain to reduce cascade evictions.

2026-03-09: Converged on upgrade strategy: staggered replace in waves of 5% of nodes with a 10m observation window, with automatic rollback if GPUDriverCrashLoop or >2% increase in PodPending for the namespace 'ml-inference' is detected.

2026-03-11: Security review passed for IAM scope required by launch templates (least-privilege role documented). Need final approvals for enabling 'mixed_instance_fallback' by default in Dedicated customer rollouts.

2026-03-12: Implemented initial Terraform interface and published module draft at registry path registry.internal/redwood/gpu-node-tier. Next: add CI e2e tests and a canary deploy to staging-cluster-a.
technical_decisions: Expose single module with two feature flags: enable_asg_flow and enable_karpenter_flow. Only one flow should be active per deployment to avoid conflicting scale signals.
Use lifecycle hooks for ASG to run 'pre-terminate' script that hits /healthz on the node's kubelet and runs 'nvidia-smi -L' to validate GPU exposed before drain begins.

For Karpenter, add a small controller (sidecar in provisioner namespace) that validates node readiness post-provision and annotates nodes to allow our rolling-upgrade operator to detect externally-provisioned nodes.
Support mixed instance type lists and an optional 'preferred_order' list to control SKU selection for constrained-fallback behavior.

Driver upgrades will be delivered via a DaemonSet with image pinning and 'preflight' initContainers that validate kernel module compatibility; the module will create the CRD-based upgrade-job to coordinate the waves.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Dual autoscalers (ASG + Karpenter) could fight resulting in oscillation. Mitigation: module validation fails if both flags enabled; document recommended workflows for hybrid clusters.
Risk: GPU driver mismatch during upgrades causing crashloops. Mitigation: preflight test + canary images + automated rollback when DriverCrashLoop detected

Risk: ENI/subnet exhaustion blocking scale up. Mitigation: add subnet capacity checks in preflight and provision ENI headroom metric alerting. If threshold crossed, module can optionally burst to a non-GPU pool for lower-priority workloads.
Risk: Long pod eviction times for large batch jobs. Mitigation: support 'eviction_protection' label for namespaces or pods; module will not drain nodes with protected pods unless forced.

Wire Datadog dashboard: NodeGPUUtilization, PodPendingByReason, DriverCrashLoopCount
Complete runbook for performing manual rollback of a botched driver rollout
Add examples to module README for ASG-only and Karpenter-only deployments in private VPC with sample HCL configs
testing_notes: Staging tests executed on staging-cluster-a; observed expected fallback to smaller GPU SKU when primary SKU capacity was exhausted in 'us-west-2-private-subnet-b'.
Simulated driver mismatch using 'driver-test' image; preflight caught incompatibility and aborted wave automatically.
Load test: sustained 1k concurrent inference pods on medium GPU nodes; module's suggested autoscaler profile kept 95th-percentile pod scheduling latency under 350ms.
